rounds.text: Alacrity Securities Ltd is notably under-appreciated given its intrinsic valuation, where a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 87 per share against a market price of ₹ 66.1, providing a solid margin of safety of 24.3% [E2, E43, E44]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF demonstrates that today's market price only implies a 14.1% earnings growth rate, which is overly conservative when compared against the base case assumption of 18.0% and the company's historical compounding profit growth of 20% over 10 years and 25% over 5 years [E18, E19, E45]. The business also exhibits elite cash-generation capabilities, evidenced by a massive cash conversion of 5.17x for March 2026 where operating cash flows reached Rs 31 Cr and free cash flow hit Rs 30 Cr, meaning profits are fully backed by hard cash [E34, E35, E36]. Operationally, the firm outperforms sector benchmarks significantly, delivering an ROA of 7.62% versus the sector benchmark of -0.45%, an ROCE of 9.43% against a sector benchmark of 4.44%, and robust 10-year compounded sales growth of 25% [E8, E10, E14]. Conceded: Promoter holdings have dropped by 11.39 percentage points over the last few years, and the trailing twelve months reflect a temporary contraction in sales growth of -18% and profit growth of -14% [E17, E21, E41].

Alacrity Securities Ltd carries fundamental vulnerabilities and valuation risks that are masked by short-term metrics, starting with a troubling deterioration in top-line and bottom-line growth over the trailing twelve months, where compounded sales growth dropped to -18% and profit growth fell to -14% [E17, E21]. Compounding these growth contractions is a concerning insider trend, as promoter holdings have dropped significantly by 11.39 percentage points over recent years from 65.73% down to 54.34% [E41]. Furthermore, despite reporting repeated profits, the company stubbornly distributes a 0.00% dividend yield to shareholders [E4, E60]. Operational efficiency is also sliding, evidenced by an operating margin that contracted by 2 percentage points from 5% to 3% over the TTM period alongside an inconsistent yearly margin trend [E30, E32]. Compounding these operational hurdles, the stock exhibits extreme volatility of 56.8% and carries a severe historical drawdown risk with a worst peak-to-trough drop of -75.1% [E51, E52]. Conceded: the company maintains a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.10x alongside strong recent cash conversion metrics [E34, E38].

Conceded: compounded sales and profit growth contracted over the trailing twelve months by -18% and -14% respectively [E17, E21], but these short-term dips are entirely overshadowed by robust multi-year records of 25% annualized sales growth and 20% to 25% profit growth over 3, 5, and 10-year spans [E14, E15, E16, E18, E19, E20]. While promoter holdings adjusted over a three-year period [E61], insiders still retain a majority stake of 54.34% [E41]. Conceded: the company pays a 0.00% dividend yield [E4], yet this capital is retained within a conservatively financed balance sheet featuring a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.10x alongside exceptional cash generation where operating cash flow reached Rs 31 Cr and covered profit by 5.17x in March 2026 [E34, E35, E38]. Although margins experienced a slight TTM compression [E30], the business operates inside a robust financial services tailwind scoring +0.83 where its ROCE of 9.43% comfortably beats the sector median of 6.1% [E10, E71, E74]. Finally, the cited historical volatility and drawdown [E51, E52] are mitigated by a strong relative-strength rating of 76 against the Nifty 500 and a discounted cash flow valuation showing a substantial 24.3% margin of safety [E44, E49].
